title: Camper Rental Station Manager - Oslo (Near Gardermoen Airport)
description:
Station Manager -- Oslo (Near Gardermoen Airport)

Arctic Campers AS is looking for an experienced, motivated, and hands-on Station Manager to take responsibility for the daily operation of our Oslo station, located close to Gardermoen Airport.

As Station Manager, you will be responsible for ensuring that customers receive an outstanding experience, employees have the support they need to succeed, and our fleet of camper vans is always prepared to the highest standard.

This is a leadership position for someone who enjoys taking responsibility, leading people by example, and being actively involved in the daily operation rather than managing only from an office.

The position is full-time and starts at the beginning of January.

Training

Before taking over responsibility for the Oslo station, you will complete a mandatory 2.5 month training program at our headquarters in Tromsø.

During this period you will learn every aspect of our operation, including:

  • Customer service and camper van handovers

  • Fleet preparation and quality control

  • Vehicle logistics

  • Camper van equipment and technical systems

  • Daily station management

  • Company procedures and operational standards

Accommodation during the training period in Tromsø will be provided by Arctic Campers.

Our working language is English, and you will become part of an international team consisting of colleagues from many different countries.

Educational and Skill Requirements

  • Previous leadership or management experience is an advantage

  • A minimum of 10 years of work experience in any profession is considered a strong advantage

  • Experience from tourism, vehicle rental, hospitality, logistics, automotive, or a similar industry is preferred

  • Experience leading and developing employees is an advantage

  • Interest in camper vans, tourism, and customer service

  • Basic technical understanding of vehicles or camper vans is an advantage

  • Valid Category B driver's licence (BE licence is an advantage)

  • Excellent English language skills (additional languages are an advantage)

  • Strong organizational and communication skills

  • Independent, structured, and solution-oriented working style

  • Positive attitude, honesty, reliability, and willingness to take responsibility

Main Responsibilities

  • Managing the daily operation of the Oslo station

  • Leading, motivating, and supporting the station team

  • Onboarding, training, and supervising permanent and seasonal employees

  • Participating in the daily operation alongside your team whenever required

  • Ensuring professional customer service and high-quality camper van handovers

  • Planning and coordinating daily staffing and operational activities

  • Maintaining an overview of the camper van fleet together with the Head of Operations and Fleet Manager

  • Coordinating vehicle movements between stations and workshops

  • Ensuring all camper vans meet Arctic Campers' quality standards before every rental

  • Monitoring and maintaining the station's technical equipment, tools, and facilities

  • Supporting troubleshooting of camper van equipment and coordinating repairs when necessary

  • Ensuring company procedures, safety standards, and operational routines are followed

  • Reporting operational performance, challenges, and improvement opportunities to management

  • Continuously improving station efficiency and customer satisfaction

  • Performing other operational and administrative tasks as required

Working Hours

This is a full-time permanent position.

Working hours are scheduled according to operational requirements and will include weekends and public holidays during the rental season.

Working Permit

Arctic Campers AS welcomes applications from both Norwegian residents and international candidates.

  • Norwegian citizens: No work permit is required.

  • EU/EEA citizens: We will assist with the necessary paperwork required to register and work legally in Norway.

  • Non-EU/EEA citizens: We do not sponsor work visas or residence permits. Applicants who require visa sponsorship are unfortunately not eligible for this position and should not apply.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Arctic Campers AS is one of Norway's largest camper van rental companies, with stations in Tromsø and Oslo. Every year we welcome thousands of travellers from all over the world who choose our custom-built camper vans to explore Norway's spectacular landscapes.

We are a young, international company where teamwork, responsibility, and continuous improvement are highly valued. We believe that great customer experiences begin with great employees, and we are looking for a Station Manager who shares that mindset.

If you are looking for a challenging leadership position where no two days are the same, enjoy working with people, and want to be part of an ambitious and growing company, we would love to hear from you.

title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Arctic Humanities, Arctic infrastructure studies and GIS
description:
The position

A three-year Postdoctoral Research Fellow position is available at the School of Business and Economics (Handelshøgskolen), UiT The Arctic University of Norway, starting 1 March 2027. 

The position is affiliated with the Research Council of Norway Groundbreaking research funded project ROADS – The Roads That Remain: Residual Pathways as Living Archives in Northern Fennoscandia (2026-2030), led by Dr. Tarja Salmela. 

We are seeking a researcher with expertise in GIS, spatial analysis, and critical approaches to mapping and infrastructure, and interest towards collaborative, experimental, and community-oriented research methods. The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary and internationally oriented research team investigating how roads and pathways continue to shape Northern landscapes long after their official purpose has faded, alongside pathways that are less visible in the landscape yet continue to endure through local knowledge, ongoing practices of movement, and memory. 

The appointment is for a period of three years, ending 28 February 2030. It is a prerequisite that the applicant can carry out the project over the full course of the employment period. No person may hold more than one fixed term position as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the same institution.

As a Postdoctoral Research Fellow, you will have the opportunity to advance your scientific career and further qualify for academic positions. If you do not already have the educational competence that meets the requirements for an Associate Professor position in Norway, UiT will arrange such competence during the employment period.

The workplace is at UiT in Tromsø. You must be able to start in the position within a reasonable time after receiving the offer.

Working and living in Tromsø 

Tromsø/Romssa serves as an important hub for research, culture, governance, and mobility in the region of Northern Norway and Sápmi. Its position as a regional gateway between coastal, inland, and cross-border northern landscapes makes it a particularly meaningful base for ROADS. 

The School of Business and Economics at UiT hosts a growing community of scholars working on sustainability, governance, mobilities, Arctic transformations, and societal change. The successful candidate will become part of a dynamic interdisciplinary environment, including UiT’s Environmental Humanities thematic network that ROADS is closely connected to.


The project/position's field of research

The project 

ROADS offers the first systematic study of residual road infrastructures in Northern Fennoscandia—roads and pathways that have fallen out of official purpose but continue to shape landscapes, memories, and mobility practices across the region. These include bypassed roads, abandoned transport corridors, former military and extractive infrastructures, and old roads and seasonal pathways embedded within local and Sámi land-use traditions.

While many remain visible in the landscape, their histories increasingly persist through local knowledge systems that risk disappearing as generations pass. Rather than approaching such infrastructures as obsolete remnants, ROADS conceptualizes them as living archives: material traces through which memory, power, mobility, resistance, and future possibilities continue to unfold.

Drawing on feminist and decolonial Science and Technology Studies, critical infrastructure studies, political ecology, environmental humanities and Indigenous ontologies, ROADS seeks to broaden conventional understandings of infrastructure by integrating relational, seasonal, and more-than human mobility systems into analyses of northern landscapes.

The project combines GIS-based spatial analysis, archival research, ethnography, repeat photography and artistic methods, and collaborative countermapping. It is grounded in close collaboration with local and Sámi communities and culminates in community-responsive public outputs, including a multilingual digital storymap and participatory mapping platform.

While GIS and spatial analysis provide important analytical foundations, ROADS combines these approaches with ethnographic, archival, visual, and artistic methods. The project therefore welcomes applicants interested in methodological experimentation and interdisciplinary research across the social sciences, humanities, environmental sciences, and arts.

The postdoctoral project and responsibilities

The Postdoctoral Research Fellow will play a central role in the project and contribute to both its analytical and public-facing outputs. 

The postdoctoral researcher will lead the spatial and archival components of Work Package 1: Tracing the temporal lives of residual and rendered invisible infrastructures and contribute to synthesis and engagement activities in Work Package 3: Reimagining residual road infrastructures and mobilities in Northern Fennoscandia.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Conducting GIS-based spatial analysis of residual road infrastructures across Northern Fennoscandia.
  • Integrating historical maps, infrastructure records, aerial imagery, and satellite data to identify and visualize infrastructural change over time.
  • Developing innovative approaches to critical spatial visualization and mapping that foreground questions of memory, erasure, survivance, and infrastructural power.
  • Contributing to archival research and the interpretation of historical infrastructure records. 
  • Participating in ethnographic fieldwork, collaborative mapping activities, repeat photography, and visual documentation initiatives alongside the Principal Investigator.
  • Co-leading participatory countermapping workshops and contributing to the development of a multilingual digital storymap and other public facing outputs.
  • Publishing research findings in leading international journals and contributing to conferences, outreach activities, and project dissemination. 

The position offers an opportunity to engage with northern landscapes and communities across Northern Fennoscandia in a place-sensitive way. Fieldwork will take place in active collaboration with local and Sámi knowledge holders and cultural institutions. The postdoctoral researcher will contribute to research that is attentive to the diverse histories, experiences, and knowledge systems that shape northern mobility landscapes.

The postdoctoral researcher will work closely with the Principal Investigator while also developing an independent research profile within the broader framework of the project.


Project description requirements

Applicants are asked to submit a project description (3–5 pages) outlining how they would approach the responsibilities of the postdoctoral position outlined above, within ROADS. The description should demonstrate the applicant's understanding of the project's aims and explain how they would contribute to the spatial, archival, and interdisciplinary dimensions of the research. The description must include a progress plan. 

Applicants are encouraged to reflect on relevant theoretical perspectives, methodological approaches, and analytical strategies, including the use of GIS, spatial analysis, historical sources, participatory mapping, and interdisciplinary collaboration where appropriate. The description should also indicate how the applicant's expertise and research interests would contribute to the project's broader objectives while supporting the development of an independent research profile within the ROADS framework.


Contact

For further information about the position, please contact:

Dr. Tarja Salmela, Principal Investigator, ROADS
email: tarja.t.salmela@uit.no  
School of Business and Economics, BFE 
UiT The Arctic University of Norway


Qualifications

Required qualifications: 

  • A PhD or equivalent degree in geography, GIScience, human geography, spatial humanities, environmental humanities, infrastructure studies, archaeology, heritage studies, Indigenous studies, anthropology, planning, landscape studies, digital humanities, or another relevant discipline. If you’re at the final stages of your PhD, you may still apply if you have submitted your PhD thesis for doctoral degree evaluation within the application deadline. You must submit the thesis with your application. Documentation of your completed PhD degree must be submitted before commencement.
  • Expertise in GIS and spatial analysis.
  • Experience working with spatial datasets, historical maps, remote sensing data, or related geospatial materials. 
  • Strong academic publication record relative to career stage. 
  • Proficiency in spoken and written English. Nordic applicants can document their capabilities by attaching their high school diploma.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing actively to collaborative research environments.

Desired qualifications: 

  • Skills in Norwegian, Swedish, Finnish, or a Sámi language are considered an asset. We also value applicants who are motivated to develop language skills relevant to the project's geographical and cultural contexts.
  • Experience with critical GIS, participatory mapping, countermapping, or spatial humanities approaches.
  • Knowledge of Arctic, Northern, Indigenous, environmental, infrastructure, mobility, landscape, or heritage research.
  • Experience integrating qualitative and quantitative spatial methods.
  • Skills in visual storytelling, cartographic design, digital heritage, digital humanities, or multimedia research dissemination. 
  • Experience conducting archival research and working with historical sources. 
  • Interest in interdisciplinary and creative research methods, including visual, arts-based, or experimental approaches to landscape and infrastructure research. 
  • Experience working across disciplinary boundaries and integrating spatial, archival, ethnographic, visual, or participatory methods.
  • Familiarity with community-based research, collaborative knowledge production, and Indigenous methodologies

ROADS is grounded in long-term collaboration with local and Sámi communities and engages critically with Indigenous knowledge systems and questions of self-determination and cultural heritage. Sámi scholars and other Indigenous scholars, as well as applicants with relevant experience working in Indigenous research contexts, are particularly encouraged to apply. We also encourage applications from researchers whose experiences and perspectives can contribute to the project's commitment to plurality, community engagement, and inclusive knowledge production.

In the assessment the main emphasis will be attached to the submitted works and the project proposal for the qualifying work. Emphasis shall also be attached to experience from popularization/dissemination and academic policy and administrative activity.

During the assessment emphasis will be put on the candidate’s motivation, potential for research, and personal suitability for the position. We are looking for candidates who:

  • Have good collaboration skills
  • Have good communication and interaction with colleagues and students
  • Wants to contribute to a good working environment

At UiT we put emphasis on the quality, relevance and significance of the research work and not on where the work is published, in accordance with the principles of The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA).


Inclusion and diversity  

UiT The Arctic University i Norway is working actively to promote equality, gender balance and diversity among employees and students, and to create an inclusive and safe working environment. We believe that inclusion and diversity is a strength, and we want employees with different competencies, professional experience, life experience and perspectives.  

If you have a disability, a gap in your CV or immigrant background, we encourage you to tick the box for this in your application. If there are qualified applicants, we invite least one in each group for an interview. If you get the job, we will adapt the working conditions if you need it. Apart from selecting the right candidates, we will only use the information for anonymous statistics. 


We offer

The successful candidate will join an internationally connected and intellectually vibrant research environment at UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Handelshøgskolen, and the thematic network of Environmental Humanities at UiT. The successful candidate will become part of an innovative research project addressing pressing questions concerning infrastructure, mobility, cultural heritage, and environmental change in the Arctic.

The position offers:

  • The opportunity to contribute to a research project with strong academic and societal relevance.
  • Close collaboration with researchers working across Arctic studies, mobility studies, infrastructure studies, environmental humanities, Indigenous studies, heritage research, and critical geography.
  • Opportunities for international collaboration, conference participation, publication, and career development.
  • Access to GIS and research infrastructure through UiT.
  • Significant opportunities to develop a strong academic research profile.
  • Good career opportunities 
  • Flexible working hours and a state collective pay agreement  
  • Pension scheme through the state pension fund 

Norwegian health policy aims to ensure that everyone, irrespective of their personal finances and where they live, has access to good health and care services of equal standard. As an employee you will become member of the National Insurance Scheme which also include health care services.

More practical information for working and living in Norway can be found here: https://uit.no/staffmobility 


Application

Please note that the application will only be assessed based on the information submitted by the application deadline via Jobbnorge. It is therefore important that you include all necessary documents demonstrating your qualifications for the position.

Your application must include:

  • Letter of motivation
  • Project proposal (3–5 pages)
  • Academic CV
  • Diplomas and transcripts (all degrees)
  • Documentation of English proficiency
  • Contact information to 2-3 references
  • Documentation of educational competence, if available
  • Description of your academic production, stating which works you consider most important
  • Publication list
  • Academic works, up to ten. The doctoral thesis is regarded as one work.

If you’re at the final stages of your PhD, you may still apply if you have submitted your PhD thesis for doctoral degree evaluation within the application deadline. You must submit the thesis with your application. Documentation of your completed PhD degree must be submitted before commencement.

All documentation to be considered must be in a Scandinavian language or English. If English proficiency is not documented in the application, it must be documented before starting in the position.


Assessment

The applicants will be assessed by an expert committee. The committee's mandate is to undertake an assessment of the applicants' qualifications based on the written material presented by the applicants, and the detailed description draw up for the position. A copy of the assessment report will be sent to all applicants. 

The applicants who are assessed as best qualified will be called to an interview. The interview should among other things, aim to clarify the applicant’s motivation and personal suitability for the position. A trial lecture may also be held.


General information

The appointment is made in accordance with State regulations and guidelines at UiT. At our website, you will find more information for applicants. 

The remuneration for Postdoctoral research fellow is in accordance with the State salary scale code 1352 with a gross annual salary ranging from NOK 630 000 to 720 000 (in a 100% position). (In special cases, a higher salary may be considered.) A compulsory contribution of 2 % to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted. You will become a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund, which gives you many benefits in addition to a lifelong pension. Read more about your employee benefits at: spk.no.

The successful candidate must be willing to get involved in the ongoing development of their department and the university as a whole.

UiT wishes to promote gender equality. If two or more applicants are found to be equally qualified, the university will rank applicants from the underrepresented gender ahead of others.

According to the Norwegian Freedom and Information Act (Offentleglova) information about the applicant may be included in the public applicant list, also in cases where the applicant has requested non-disclosure. 


Om arbeidsgiveren:

UiT The Arctic University of Norway is a multi-campus research university and the northernmost university of the world. Our central location in the High North, our broad and diverse research and study portfolio, and our interdisciplinary qualities make us uniquely suited to meet the challenges of the future. At UiT you can explore global issues from a close-up perspective.

Credibility, academic freedom, closeness, creativity and commitment shall be hallmarks of the relationship between our employees, between our employees and our students and between UiT and our partners. 

The Faculty of Biosciences, Fisheries and Economics (BFE) consists of Department of Arctic and Marine Biology, Norwegian College of Fishery Science (NFH) and School of Business and Economics.The main task of BFE is to conduct teaching and research dissemination at a high national and international level within all relevant fields. Prioritized research areas are aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems, climate, life in the arctic, marine bioprospecting, fish health, seafood products, business and macroeconomics, resources and environment, markets and management of marine resources. The interdisciplinary profile of the faculty provides good opportunity to develop research projects involving several research groups at the faculty according to its strategy.

Ei variert rolle der du får ein viktig funksjon i den daglege drifta av teknologiparken og bidreg til at både besøkande og leigetakarar får ei god oppleving.

Hva vi ser etter

Vi ønskjer ein person som:

  • Er strukturert og sjølvstendig

  • Har gode samarbeidsevner og eit positivt vesen

  • Likar å yte god service og skape gode opplevingar for andre

  • Er fleksibel og trivst med varierte arbeidsoppgåver

  • Tek initiativ og ser kva som trengst å gjerast

Arbeidsoppgaver

  • Vere vertskap for besøkande og gjester i Årdal Teknologipark

  • Koordinere bookingar og leggje til rette for møte, kurs og arrangement

  • Fakturering og enklare administrative oppgåver

  • Informere brukarar og besøkande om rutinar og retningslinjer i lokala

  • Bidra til orden, trivsel og god service i teknologiparken

  • Andre førefallande administrative og praktiske oppgåver

Vi tilbyr

  • Ei variert og sjølvstendig stilling i eit spennande næringsmiljø

  • Eit godt arbeidsmiljø med engasjerte menneske

  • Moglegheit til å vere med og vidareutvikle Årdal Teknologipark

  • Løn etter avtale

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Vi skal legge til rette for ny industri og næring i Årdal gjennom bygg, areal, infrastruktur og teknologi, samt koordinere og støtte samarbeid mellom eksisterande og nye aktørar i Årdal og regionen.

Våre eigarar er Årdal Utvikling, Hydro Aluminium og Årdal Energi Holding. I saman sikrar vi trygg tilrettelegging for industri- og næringsutvikling i Årdal med ei veksande eigedomsportefølje.

Selskapet arbeider tett og koordinert saman med Årdal Utvikling og Sitep, med eit felles mål om å sikre eit meir robust næringsliv i kommunen. Arbeidet vårt er forankra i det lokale næringslivet og vi er ein pådrivar for samarbeid og etablering.

Her har vi samla eit mangfald av kompetansebedrifter innan eit breitt spekter av fagområde, alt frå gründerbedrifter som produserer alger til Hydro sitt senter for forsking- og teknologiutvikling innan aluminiumsproduksjon.

title: Crunched (YC-backed 25)- Growth Manager
description:
Crunched - Growth Manager (Oslo)

Location: Oslo, Norway (forward-deployed with customers, regular international travel)

Type: Full-time

Compensation: Competitive salary + equity

Stage: YC-backed, 55M NOK seed, building our core team out of Oslo

Define how the world's largest advisory firms adopt AI

Crunched is building the world's most powerful AI analyst for strategy and corporate finance workflows -- autonomous, agent-based AI that works directly inside Excel, where half of the world's business decisions are made. We're backed by Y Combinator, raised 55M NOK in seed funding, and our product is already trusted by professionals at firms like BCG, BDO, CBRE, Dentsu, Pareto, PwC, INSEAD and Harvard.

Why Crunched can win

Large AI platforms like Anthropic are serious competitors. Crunched is different because we build deeply for the top 1--2% of Excel power users and their highly specific workflows. In every direct customer evaluation against competing products so far, Crunched has won on quality. First Round heard pitches from 75 AI-for-Excel startups over the past year---and chose to invest in Crunched.

We're growing extremely quickly inside large international accounts. The Growth Manager is our most important hire right now -- the first dedicated go-to-market and customer success role at the company. You'll be embedded with our biggest customers across countries: developing the accounts, driving adoption, and building custom workflows alongside the people who use Crunched every day.

This is a core position. Being forward-deployed with customers is at the heart of how we build.

What you'll do

  • Own and grow our most strategic enterprise accounts from day one

  • Onboard new customers, teams and offices, and drive real adoption and ROI

  • Expand usage inside large advisory firms -- new offices, new teams, new use cases (for example, rolling Crunched out across new PwC offices)

  • Work closely with our tech team, turning what you learn in the field into bespoke solutions and product improvements

  • Build custom workflows alongside the analysts and consultants who use Crunched daily

  • Help open new markets across Europe, with Germany a key focus

  • Build the customer success / growth function and team as we scale

Who you are

  • Real drive and unrelenting structure -- you operate independently and own outcomes end-to-end

  • A strong interest in AI and how it is reshaping knowledge work

  • The judgment and presence to work with senior stakeholders at the world's largest advisory firms

  • Comfortable being forward-deployed and traveling to customers across borders

Best fit

A background in MBB-style management consulting , or several years in customer success at a high standard. Prior growth or customer success experience is preferred, but a strong consulting or finance background is a major asset -- it gives you credibility and a deep understanding of how our customers actually work. Experience from a customer-type firm (e.g. BDO, CBRE, Dentsu, Pareto, PwC) is a strong plus.


What you get

  • Ownership of our most important accounts from day one

  • A mandate to define how the world's largest advisory firms adopt AI

  • The opportunity to build the function and team as we scale

  • A hands-on product that delivers real productivity and ROI -- with genuine differentiators like EU data residency and best-in-class PowerPoint generation

  • Very competitive compensation: salary + equity from day one, with additional upside tied to our largest accounts open for discussion

  • Regular travel to customers across borders

Working model

Based in our Oslo office, forward-deployed with customers and traveling regularly across Norway and Europe. If you want to be close to customers and the core team while building something at high speed, this is for you.

title: Project Controller
description:
Kongsberg Maritime is looking for a Project Controller to join our Energy & Control, Finance team. In this role, you will play a key part in ensuring strong financial control and support throughout the lifecycle of our projects.

As Project Controller, you will work closely with Project Managers and colleagues across Finance, Sales, Delivery and Product management. You will contribute to delivering high-quality financial insights, maintaining project profitability, and supporting successful project execution.


What you will be doing
• Be an active member of the Project Controller team
• Establish projects in ERP systems and maintain project budgets
• Perform invoicing and crediting activities
• Support month-end closing activities, including revenue and cost recognition
• Prepare monthly project reporting and participate in project reviews
• Identify and evaluate financial risks and opportunities
• Provide financial support and analysis to project teams and stakeholders
• Contribute to continuous improvement and other ad hoc tasks within the Finance team

We're looking for someone who's service-minded, flexible, and eager for new challenges. If, you are someone who loves being given responsibility and can communicate clearly, we would like to hear from you!

We are continuously reviewing applications, apply today!


We think you should have
• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related field
• Understanding of commercial and contractual aspects of project business
• Strong Excel skills and experience working with ERP systems
• Experience from a similar finance or project controlling role is an advantage
• Good written and verbal communication skills in English

At Kongsberg Maritime, we believe that diversity fuels innovation. We encourage you to apply, even if you do not meet every requirement. Your unique perspective is valuable to us. Your skills, attitude and perspective could be exactly what we are looking for!


You are able to
• act on own initiative, make things happen and accept responsibility for the results.
• focus on bottom-line results, identify potential risks and monitor the financial impact of own activities.
• comply with company rules and procedures and execute plans with commitment and determination.
• use a methodical and systematic approach, plan ahead, define clear priorities and allocate resources effectively.
• communicate in a clear, precise and structured way.
• co-operate well with others, share knowledge, experience, information and support others in the pursuit of team goals.
If you're ready to take on this exciting challenge, apply now and become a part of our team!

This employment may require a pre-employment check procedure in accordance with company security standards, role or site requirements. Please note that this might affect the offer process or employment.


What we can offer you
With us, you will be offered a competitive salary and benefits package, along with development opportunities in an international environment. We offer flexible working hours, good pension & insurance schemes, and an inclusive supportive work environment. You will have the opportunity to work with sustainable and forward-looking solutions in the maritime industry.

Work location
Kongsberg, Sandefjord, Horten.

Point of contact
Liv Frøvold, Manager Project Controlling, +47 909 92 865. liv.frovold@km.kongsberg.com.


Kongsberg Maritime is a global leader in maritime technology. We deliver advanced solutions to the merchant fleet, offshore, fishing, and naval vessels, setting new standards for safe, efficient, and sustainable operations - both for new builds and existing fleets. In close collaboration with customers and research environments, we develop technology that solves real challenges at sea. Today, more than 30,000 vessels operate with our systems on board. Kongsberg Maritime has more than 8,300 employees in 35 countries.

Technologies for sustainable oceans

Energy & Control brings together Kongsberg Maritime’s strengths in Vessel Automation & Sensing Solutions, Offshore Production, Ship Design & Integration, Bridge & Remote and Electrical Systems to deliver smart, integrated solutions across the ocean space. From single products to fully integrated systems, we help customers improve efficiency, reliability and sustainability, enabling the maritime energy transition. Our global teams operate end-to-end, from sales through product development and engineering to project execution - making us a trusted partner for yards, ship owners and operators across segments.

title: Associate Professor in Geomechanics and Geohazards
description:
About the Department and what they are looking for in this position

We invite applications for a full time position as Associate Professor in Geomechanics & Geohazards is available at the Department of Geosciences.

The Department of Geosciences (GEO) at the University of Oslo is part of the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Science and is a leading research unit in Europe. The Department covers a wide breadth of topics, from mantle and lithosphere dynamics on Earth and other planets, via surface processes in the boundary layers between Earth’s surface and atmosphere, to the dynamics and interactions in the Earth's crust, soils, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere.

The Department of Geosciences has defined a strategy focusing on four main themes that cut across the Department:

1.    Dynamics of the solid Earth and planets
2.    Climate change and the coupled Earth system
3.    Environmental geosciences
4.    Geoscience in the Arctic

The Department aims to contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and hosts important contributors to the IPCC (UN Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change).

The staff consists of approximately 40 professors and associate professors, in addition to postdoctoral fellows, PhD candidates, researchers, and technical and administrative staff. In total, the Department currently has around 200 employees, one Centre of Excellence and, at present, seven grants from the European Research Council (ERC), along with numerous other grants from public and private institutions. The Department is organized in six sections:

  • Basin Studies
  • Crustal Processes
  • Centre for Planetary Habitability [PHAB, Centre of Excellence]
  • Environmental Geoscience
  • Physical Geography and Hydrology
  • Meteorology and Oceanography

and a group in geoscience didactics. The Department offers two bachelor study programmes “Geology and Geography” and “Geophysics and Climate” and one MSc-programme in “Geosciences”. 

This position is primarily associated with the Crustal Processes section that mostly works with geological processes related to rock deformation (fracture, friction, creep), fluid flow in crustal rocks (water, gas, magma), and fluid-rock interactions. Researchers develop studies from the atomic scale to the lithospheric scale, with applications in the domains of Solid Earth geohazards, porous media, critical raw materials, and large-scale tectonics. Research in the section uses field work, analytical and imaging techniques, modelling, data science, and experiments, and aims to unravel the processes that shape the evolution of the Earth’s crust, and their effects on the environment. The section consists of 40 people, and at present is organised under a Faculty centre between Geoscience and Physics (Njord Centre).


General information about the position

Applicants must document academic qualifications in their field at a level equivalent to an Associate Professor. The position will be based at the University of Oslo. The successful candidate must be able to teach at all levels and supervise Master’s and PhD students. The successful candidate may also be required to take on other teaching duties and administrative tasks when requested by the Department or the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences. The working time in the position is divided approximately as follows: 45% research, 45% education, and 10% administrative tasks.

The position is closely linked to the Department’s strategy by contributing to “research-based knowledge with societal relevance linked to climate, environment, energy, natural hazards, and sustainable use of resources”. The duties therefore include research, teaching, supervision, and dissemination/communication within both geomechanics and geohazards. The position will serve as a link between the Department’s expertise in various research fields relevant to geohazards (including geophysics, geomechanics, geomorphology, hydrology, hydrogeology and environmental geology). One of our aims is to advance the understanding of slow and rapid rock mass and granular material movements by developing and applying advanced methods and models that contribute to solving fundamental scientific and societal challenges related to geohazards.


Your main tasks will be

Your main research-related tasks will be:

  • Conduct cutting-edge fundamental research with broad international impact in geomechanics with applications to geohazards (earthquakes, landslides, and other gravitational instabilities).
  • Develop advanced numerical models for improving the simulation, the analysis, and the prediction of geohazards, as well as the application of tools and concepts from other disciplines (e.g. physics, data science) to geomechanics.
  • Attract substantial external research funding (e.g., from EU Horizon programmes, the Research Council of Norway, the Norwegian Directorate for Water Resources and Energy, and related funding bodies).
  • Promote collaboration with external partners such as the Norwegian Geotechnical Institute (NGI), the Norwegian Seismic Array (NORSAR), and other relevant institutions.
     

Your main teaching-related tasks will be to actively contribute to teaching at both bachelor’s and master’s level in topics related to geomechanics and geohazards, including landslides in granular materials and water/rock interactions. At present, the following 10 ECTS courses are offered at the Department of Geosciences: 

  • GEO3034 (Geohazards)
  • GEO4131 (Geomechanics) 
  • GEO4151 (Earthquakes and Volcanoes)
  • GEO4171 (Floods, Avalanches, Landslides) 

The candidate is expected to take primary responsibility for up to two courses and supervise master’s theses in these subject areas. Course responsibility does not imply giving all lectures, but to organise lectures and lab-exercises in the course. Experience and/or interest in fieldwork is also desirable.

We expect mainly physical attendance at the University of Oslo.


More information about the position

Applicants must document academic qualifications in their field, equivalent to an Associate professor position. The successful applicant must be able to teach at all levels and to supervise Master and PhD students. 

The successful applicant may furthermore be required to take on other teaching duties and administrative tasks, by request from the Department or the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences. 


What skills are important in this role?

Assessment of candidates will be based on scientific and educational excellence, as for example reflected in the quality of peer-reviewed publications, scientific relevance, ability to attract external funding, and other evidence of impact. The main emphasis will be on the candidate’s performance during the last five years. We expect the candidate having a scientific track record at a high international level that demonstrates the ability to fund and lead research projects.

Required qualifications:

  • The successful applicant must have completed a PhD in geology, geomechanics, or geophysics or related fields, with a focus on e.g., geomechanics, structural geology, civil engineering or geomorphology. 
  • Documented post-doctoral or equivalent experience and a strong scientific track record within areas of the mechanics of geomaterials (solid rocks and/or granular materials), computational methods in mechanics or geophysics, and solid earth geohazards including earthquakes, landslides and other gravitational instabilities.
  • Ability to collaborate across scientific disciplines.
  • Documented potential for acquisition of external research funding.
  • Pedagogical qualifications and teaching and supervision experience at all levels will be an important factor in the evaluation process and should be well documented in a teaching portfolio. The applicant should describe her/his qualifications in view of the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) framework which includes:
    • Focus on student learning
    • A clear development over time
    • A researching approach
    • A collegial attitude and practice
  • The successful candidate who at the time of appointment cannot document sufficient teaching qualifications (minimum formal requirement is a 200 hours pedagogical programme) will be required to obtain such qualifications within a two-year period.
  • The successful candidate must demonstrate mastery of both English and one of the Scandinavian languages as working languages, in order to be able to teach and otherwise be able to participate in all functions the position may involve. If the successful candidate does not have sufficient mastery of a Scandinavian language, B2 level, the candidate will be required to learn sufficient Norwegian within  three years of employment.

Desired qualifications:

  • Candidates should be able to establish, lead and conduct research projects, also as a collaborator. 
  • An international network, experience with outreach activities, collegiality, and the ability to contribute to a good working environment.
  • Experience in scientific and administrative management, as the person appointed will be expected to take on some administrative duties.
  • Additional competences in experimental and applied and/or field studies will be considered an advantage.

All candidates and projects will have to undergo a check versus national export, sanctions and security regulations. Candidates may be excluded based on these checks. Primary checkpoints are the Export Control regulation, the Sanctions regulation, and the national security regulation.


What are we looking for in you?

Personal skills:

  • Ability to create and contribute to a well-functioning, inclusive and productive research environment
  • Strong networking skills, ability to collaborate and conduct scientific leadership
  • Ability to cooperate and communicate well with other members of staff

The successful candidate should have an international profile with respect to the above criteria. The candidate for this position will be selected based on excellence and fit with the section’s research profile.


We can offer you
  • Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organization with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development.
  • Committed colleagues in a good working environment. 
  • Good welfare schemes.
  • Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours.  A workplace with good development and career opportunities.
  • Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes.
  • Salary in position as Associate Professor (position code 1011) in salary range NOK from 850 000 - to 950 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, two % is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund. 

Inclusive work life and diversity at UiO

UiO is an open and internationally-oriented university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at UiO's policy for diversity, equality and inclusion - University of Oslo.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues, could you be the next one? We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures. 

We especially encourage women to apply.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. 

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports.

More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here.


How to apply

The application must include:

  • Application letter
  • A research position paper (max. 5 pages) describing the applicant’s vision and scientific ambitions for the nearest future
  • A detailed CV, including a complete list of education, positions, pedagogical experience, administrative management, project acquisition and coordination experience, and other qualifying activities.
  • Copies of educational certificates, PhD diploma, transcript of records and letters of recommendation
  • A complete list of publications and academic merits and awards (if not included in the CV)
  • Full text of up to 10 selected scientific publications the applicant wishes to include in the evaluation
  • A document discussing the importance, interrelation, and relevance of the selected papers for this position
  • Educational portfolio of 3–6 pages documenting educational competence and experience, including a reflection note in which your own teaching practice and view of learning is anchored in the SoTL framework (focus on student learning, development over time, a researching approach and a collegial attitude and practice) 
  • List of reference persons: 2–3 references (name, relation to candidate, e-mail and phone number)

Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.


General information

As a general rule an interview will be used in the appointment process, usually supplemented with a trial teaching session. The basis for assessment will be the scientific production of the applicant, the teaching portfolio, pedagogical and educational qualifications, the applicant’s qualifications within leadership and administration, other qualifications as well as general personal suitability for the position. In ranking the competent applicants, the full range of qualifications will be considered and explicitly assessed.

Rules for appointments to associate professorships. 
https://www.uio.no/english/about/regulations/personnel/academic/rules-appointment-professor.html

Rules for the assessment and weighting of pedagogical competence for appointments to permanent academic posts which include teaching duties: 
https://www.uio.no/english/about/regulations/personnel/academic/rules-basic-pedagogical-competence.html

Guide for applicants for Professor and Associate professor positions - University of Oslo https://www.uio.no/english/about/regulations/personnel/academic/guide-applicants.html

According to the Norwegian Freedom and Information Act (Offentleglova), information about the applicant may be included in the public applicant list, also in cases where the applicant has requested non-disclosure.

The University of Oslo has an agreement for all employees, aiming to secure rights to research results, see: http://www.uio.no/english/for-employees/employment/work-results/


Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest rated institution of research and education with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. Its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally esteemed research communities make UiO an important contributor to society. 

The geosciences are the studies of the planet Earth and its comparative planetology; the atmosphere, the hydrosphere and cryosphere, the Earth's surface and its interior. The Department of Geosciences conducts research and teaching in most of the domains of geoscience; geology, geophysics, physical geography, geomatics, hydrology, meteorology and oceanography. The Department is the broadest geoscience research and education environment in Norway. We perform research at a high international standard and have five ERC (European Research Council) research projects ongoing.

The Department encompasses six scientific sections; Meteorology and Oceanography, Geography and Hydrology, Study of sedimentary basins, Environmental geosciences. and Crustal Processes. We host now a third in the line of three Centre of Excellences:  PHAB – Centre for Planetary Habitability, and have a Norwegian Research School for PhD students (Research School for Dynamics and Evolution of Earth and Planets, DEEP).

The Department aims to contribute to the new and important UN Sustainability Development Goals, and are important contributors to IPCC (UN’s Inter-governmental Panel on Climate Change). The staff consists of 40 professors and associate professors, in addition to postdoctoral fellows, PhD students, researchers, technical- and administrative staff. The Department has around 200 employees.

title: Dintero – Senior Backend Engineer
description:
Dintero -- Senior Backend Engineer

Location: Oslo

Contact/Application: Application@yourheadway.no

Your Headway is recruiting for Dintero.

Senior backend engineer? Build payment infrastructure handling 150M+ API calls every month . At Dintero, you are not working on the edges of a product. You build core systems where failure has real consequences .

We develop and operate the entire platform ourselves and control the full payment flow. This gives us deep technical ownership, real responsibility, and engineers who influence architecture, not just implementation.

Dintero operates in a space that is complex in two dimensions:

  • Technical complexity -- distributed systems, high throughput, strict uptime requirements

  • Regulatory complexity -- payment schemes, compliance, auditability, and financial correctness


We are also at the forefront of innovation in the payment space:

  • First to implement Passkeys with Mastercard

  • Early adopters of real-time clearing APIs

  • First new acquirer in Norway in over 20 years

This is a role for engineers who want to work on serious backend systems that must work, every time .

Production at Scale

  • 150M+ API calls per month

  • 10 senior engineers -- small team, high ownership

  • Infrastructure designed for high availability and robust transaction flows

What You Will Work On

  • Design and own backend services end-to-end

  • Build APIs used directly by merchants and partners

  • Make architectural decisions with long-term impact

  • Work with scalability, observability, and operational quality

  • Ship to production frequently and take ownership of what you build

In short: less coordination, more engineering.

Tech Stack

Deliberate choices. Minimal hype.

  • AWS (Fargate, Lambda, DynamoDB, Aurora)

  • Microservices

  • Node.js and TypeScript

  • Infrastructure as Code

  • API-first

We value sound engineering decisions over chasing trends.

Your Profile

You have experience working with complex systems in production.

  • 5+ years of backend development experience

  • Experience with distributed systems and architectural trade-offs

  • Comfortable owning systems end-to-end

  • Experience where reliability, correctness, or compliance matter

  • Cloud experience (Preferably AWS)

Scandinavian language (Norwegian, Swedish, or Danish) is a plus, but not required.

This Role Is a Strong Fit If You Have Worked With

  • Payment systems or financial infrastructure

  • High-throughput APIs or event-driven systems

  • Systems with strict uptime, latency, or consistency requirements

  • Regulated domains (fintech, banking, etc.)

This Role Is Likely Not Right If You

  • Prefer frontend-focused work

  • Want heavy processes and multiple decision layers

  • Prefer narrowly defined tasks over ownership

We are intentionally a small team. Everyone contributes to core decisions.

Why Dintero

  • Real ownership of critical systems

  • Strong engineering culture -- good ideas win

  • Short decision paths

  • Work that has direct real-world impact

  • A financially solid fintech company with strong growth

Compensation

  • Competitive salary (aligned with Tekna levels)

  • Stock options

Engineers building the platform should share in the value creation.

Recruitment Process

description:
Crunched - Lead Designer (Oslo)

Location: Oslo, Norway

Type: Full-time, on-site

Design how professionals think with AI the world's most advanced AI analyst

Crunched builds autonomous AI systems that operate inside Excel-automating strategy, modelling, and financial workflows without breaking how people already work.

Our AI analyst is already used by professionals at BCG, Nordover Capital, INSEAD, Harvard, Explore, Arkwright, Connaught, and Placepoint.

We're backed by Y Combinator, have raised 55M NOK, and recently spent several months in San Francisco. Now, we're assembling the core Oslo team, and we're hiring a Senior UX Designer to own the user experience of our AI analyst.

Why Crunched can win

Large AI platforms like Anthropic are serious competitors. Crunched is different because we build deeply for the top 1--2% of Excel power users and their highly specific workflows. In every direct customer evaluation against competing products so far, Crunched has won on quality. First Round heard pitches from 75 AI-for-Excel startups over the past year---and chose to invest in Crunched.

This is not a surface-level UI role. This is about designing trust, clarity, and control in a complex, AI-driven product-embedded directly into Excel.

What you'll do

  • Own the end-to-end UX of Crunched's AI analyst-from concept to shipped product

  • Design interaction models for AI-driven workflows, not just screens

  • Apply user psychology and behavioral principles to reduce cognitive load and build trust

  • Build and evolve a systematic UX framework grounded in real user feedback

  • Design within the constraints of Excel while subtly expanding beyond it

  • Partner closely with engineers to ensure designs are feasible, performant, and shippable

  • Continuously test, learn, and iterate with real users across Europe and the US

  • Shape the long-term UX strategy and design language of Crunched

Who you are

You're a senior, strategically strong UX designer who is still deeply hands-on.

You think in systems, flows, and mental models-not just components. You enjoy getting things done and take pride in shipping work that actually changes how people operate.

You likely bring:

  • Deep understanding of user psychology and decision-making in complex tools

  • Strong experience designing data-heavy, B2B, or professional software

  • A systematic approach to UX, grounded in research, feedback loops, and iteration

  • Experience designing for AI-powered products (or complex automation tools)

  • An impeccable eye for aesthetics, leaning toward simplicity without being sterile or boring

  • Comfort working closely with engineers and product leaders in fast-moving teams

  • A high-ownership mindset and comfort with ambiguity

You don't just make things look good.

You make them make sense.

Design philosophy

At Crunched, UX is not decoration.

We care about:

  • Clarity over cleverness

  • Calm interfaces for high-stakes work

  • Power without intimidation

  • Simplicity that respects expert users

We expect strong opinions-backed by reasoning and user insight.

Compensation

We hire world-class people and compensate accordingly.

  • Competitive Salary, Depending on experience

  • Over 1M NOK in equity from day one

  • ARR-based compensation ladder where you choose between major salary increases or more equity

  • Best possible strike price allowed by legal counsel

  • Standard 4-year vesting with 1-year cliff

If you want real ownership and real upside, this is it.

We compensate well - and we expect people with the same growth ambitions and time investment required to build something truly big.

title: Part-Time Driver Alnabru
description:
We’re looking for Part-Time Drivers to join Oda!

At Oda, we develop affordable grocery services to make the logistics of living surprisingly easy. First we built Norway’s leading online grocery store and now, partnered with Mathem in Sweden, we’re on our way to becoming the world’s most effective grocery system, delivering to thousands of Scandinavian doorsteps every week.

As part of our team, you’ll work with smart, passionate colleagues who bring their whole selves to work every day. It’s a fast-moving, collaborative environment where everyone is welcome and everyone’s opinion matters. Whether you're shaping the future of online retail, tackling complex logistical problems, or making everyday life better for our customers, your work will have a real impact. Read on to find out what part you could play in our story.

What you’ll be doing as a Driver 🚚

  • Report directly to our Driver Operating Managers and Team Leaders at your site as an essential part of our dedicated delivery team.

  • Be a Customer Hero: You’ll be on the road bringing groceries and smiles directly to our customers, ensuring a top-notch "Oda experience" at every doorstep.

  • Keep the wheels turning: You’ll handle loading and unloading with speed and care, ensuring every box arrives in perfect condition.

  • Own your ride: You’ll take pride in your van, keeping it clean, presentable, and ready for the road.

  • Pay it forward: You’ll help onboard and train new colleagues, sharing your best tips and tricks from the road.

  • Make us better: We value your brain as much as your driving! You’ll contribute your ideas to help us improve our routines and ways of working.

What you’ll need to succeed 🌟

  • A valid driving license (Class B). You’ve had your license for at least 2 years and feel confident and safe behind the wheel.

  • Good communication skills: Comfortable in speaking and writing English. If you also know Norwegian or another Nordic language, that’s a big plus!

What would be nice to have 💡

  • Enjoy being active and thrive in a physically demanding job

  • Comfortable working both independently and as part of a team

  • A strong work ethic and a "can-do" mindset

  • Service-minded and always looking for the best solutions

  • A genuine desire to make our customers happy

  • Responsible and always prioritize safety in traffic

What we offer 🚀

  • A chance to make a real impact as a Part-Time Driver in a fast-moving company with a product people love-while shaking up the grocery industry.

  • Teammates who aim high and have each other’s backs. We care about people, and that means supporting each other every step of the way.

  • A flat structure where we team up across disciplines to solve exciting challenges. Big ideas come from everywhere!

  • A transparent way of working. We use Slack to stay in the loop-less email, fewer meetings, more getting things done.

  • A chance to shape the future of grocery shopping while building a company that’s here to stay.

Practical information

  • Application deadline: We review applications on an ongoing basis and may close the process once the right candidates are found. We encourage you to apply as early as possible.

  • Start date: As soon as possible.

  • Position: 20% Part-time

  • Working hours: Saturday and Sunday, every other weekend.

    • Morning shift: 05:45-13:45

    • Evening shift: 13:30-21:30

  • Location: Verkseier Furulunds Vei 1, 0668 Oslo

To ensure a fair and efficient process for everyone, we use Hubert, our virtual assistant, to help us with the first selection. 🤖 Keep an eye on your inbox – shortly after applying, you’ll receive an email with an invite to a chat-based interview. Just make sure your email address is correct so the invite finds its way to you!

A few final words

At Oda, you’ll join a passionate, ambitious team working to change the future of grocery shopping. We’re all different—just like you—and we wouldn’t have it any other way. If you need any adjustments or support during the application process, just let us know, and we’ll do our best to help. We believe in the strength of a diverse workforce and want everyone to have an equal shot at landing the job.

Come build the future of grocery with us! Want to know more about how we work? Check out these posts on Medium.

We can’t wait to hear from you! 🧡

title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Algal Microbiome Engineering
employer: UNIVERSITETET I TROMSØ - NORGES ARKTISKE UNIVERSITET UIT CAMPUS TROMSØ
description:
The position

At the Norwegian College of Fishery Science, Faculty of Biosciences, Fisheries and Economics (BFE) at UiT The Arctic University of Norway, there is a vacant position as a postdoctoral researcher affiliated with the Microalgae & Microbiomes Research Group. The position is for a fixed term of 3 years. It is a prerequisite that the applicant can carry out the project over the full course of the employment period. No person may hold more than one fixed term position as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the same institution.

The postdoctoral project focuses on programmable marine microbiomes and mechanistic interactions within the diatom phycosphere, with particular emphasis on synthetic biology, microbial ecology, and molecular interactions between marine microalgae and associated bacteria. The successful candidate will contribute to the development of experimental model systems for studying metabolite exchange, microbial community interactions, and engineered microbial consortia in marine environments.

The position is affiliated with ongoing research activities in marine microbiology, synthetic biology, and systems biology at UiT. The research combines microbiology, molecular biology, microbial cultivation, genome-informed molecular ecology, synthetic biology, and multi-omics approaches to better understand and engineer marine microbial ecosystems relevant to carbon cycling and marine biotechnology.

As a Postdoctoral Research Fellow, you will have the opportunity to advance your scientific career and further qualify for academic positions. If you do not already have the educational competence that meets the requirements for an Associate Professor position in Norway, UiT will arrange such competence during the employment period.

The workplace is at UiT in Tromsø. You must be able to start in the position within a reasonable time after receiving the offer.


The project/position's field of research

The postdoctoral researcher will develop and apply experimental approaches for studying mechanistic interactions between marine microalgae and associated bacterial communities within the diatom phycosphere. The project will focus on the development of programmable and experimentally tractable microbial model systems using synthetic biology, microbial cultivation, and molecular biology approaches.

The successful candidate will work with cultivation and engineering of marine bacteria and microalgae, construction of synthetic microbial consortia, and investigation of microbial metabolite exchange relevant to nutrient cycling and carbon fixation in marine ecosystems. The project may also involve transcriptomics, genomics, metabolomics, and bioinformatics analyses to investigate molecular interactions between diatoms and associated microorganisms.

The position is part of a broader research program focused on programmable marine microbiomes, marine microbial ecology, and biotechnology applications relevant to climate resilience, sustainable aquaculture, and marine carbon cycling. The postdoctoral researcher will work in an interdisciplinary and international research environment and is expected to contribute actively to scientific publications, collaborative research activities, and external funding development.

You must submit a project proposal (max 2 pages) that describes how you scientifically can contribute to designing diatom phycosphere communities through the uses of engineered genetic circuits or other synthetic biology tools. The proposal should include your view on the state-of-the-art and opportunities for achievable but ground-breaking science with regards to engineering microbial consortia and non-traditional synthetic biology hosts. The proposal must include a progress plan.


Contact

For further information about the position, please contact Group Leader Hans Christopher Bernstein:

  • email: hans.c.bernstein@uit.no 

 or the Head of Department Bjørn Petter Finstad: 

  • email: bjornpetter.finstad@uit.no 

Qualifications

Required qualifications: 

  • A Norwegian doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign doctoral degree recognized as equivalent to a Norwegian PhD in microbiology, molecular biology, biotechnology, synthetic biology, marine biology, microbial ecology, systems biology, chemical engineering, bioengineering, or another relevant discipline. If you're in the final stages of your PhD, you may still apply for the position, provided that you submit parts of your dissertation along with your application. This enables the evaluation committee to assess the quality and likelihood of completion by the desired employment date. You must include a statement from your supervisor or institution stating the expected completion date for your PhD degree. Documentation of your completed PhD degree must be submitted before commencement.
  • Excellent written and oral English language skills. Nordic applicants can document their capabilities by attaching their high school diploma.
  • Documented experience in experimental microbiology, molecular biology, and scientific publishing, including publication of research in peer reviewed international journals. Experience in one or more of the following areas is required:
    • synthetic biology
    • microbial cultivation
    • marine microbiology or marine microbial ecology
    • microalgae research
    • molecular cloning and genetic engineering
    • microbial ecology
    • microbial co-cultivation systems

Desired qualifications: 

  • Experience working with non-model microorganisms and/or developing molecular tools for environmental microorganisms is considered particularly advantageous.
  • Experience with one or more of the following areas is considered an advantage:
    • microbial genomics, transcriptomics, or metagenomics
    • bioinformatics and analysis of omics datasets
    • metabolomics or analytical chemistry
    • microbial community analysis
    • programming/scripting in R, Python, or similar languages
    • systems biology or computational biology
  • Knowledge of a Scandinavian language or willingness to learn Norwegian is considered an advantage.

The successful candidate must be able to work independently and as part of an interdisciplinary research team. Emphasis will also be placed on motivation, potential for research, scientific creativity, organizational skills, communication abilities, and personal suitability for the position.

In the assessment the main emphasis will be attached to the submitted works and the project proposal for the qualifying work. Emphasis shall also be attached to experience from popularization/dissemination and academic policy and administrative activity.

At UiT we put emphasis on the quality, relevance and significance of the research work and not on where the work is published, in accordance with the principles of The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA).


Inclusion and diversity  

UiT The Arctic University i Norway is working actively to promote equality, gender balance and diversity among employees and students, and to create an inclusive and safe working environment. We believe that inclusion and diversity is a strength, and we want employees with different competencies, professional experience, life experience and perspectives.  

If you have a disability, a gap in your CV or immigrant background, we encourage you to tick the box for this in your application. If there are qualified applicants, we invite least one in each group for an interview. If you get the job, we will adapt the working conditions if you need it. Apart from selecting the right candidates, we will only use the information for anonymous statistics. 


We offer
  • Involvement in an interesting research project 
  • Good career opportunities 
  • A good academic environment with dedicated colleagues  
  • Flexible working hours and a state collective pay agreement  
  • Pension scheme through the state pension fund 

Norwegian health policy aims to ensure that everyone, irrespective of their personal finances and where they live, has access to good health and care services of equal standard. As an employee you will become member of the National Insurance Scheme which also include health care services.

More practical information for working and living in Norway can be found here: https://uit.no/staffmobility 


Application

Please note that the application will only be assessed based on the information submitted by the application deadline via Jobbnorge. It is therefore important that you include all necessary documents demonstrating your qualifications for the position.

Your application must include:

  • Application letter
  • Project proposal (max 2 pages)
  • CV
  • Diplomas and transcripts (all degrees)
  • Documentation of English proficiency
  • Contact information to 2-3 references
  • Documentation of educational competence, if available
  • Description of your academic production, stating which works you consider most important
  • The academic works (published or not) you wish us to take into consideration in the assessment

If you're in the final stages of your PhD, you may still apply for the position, provided that you submit parts of your dissertation along with your application. This enables the evaluation committee to assess the quality and likelihood of completion by the desired employment date. You must include a statement from your supervisor or institution stating the expected completion date for your PhD degree. Documentation of your completed PhD degree must be submitted before commencement.

All documentation to be considered must be in a Scandinavian language or English. If English proficiency is not documented in the application, it must be documented before starting in the position. 


Assessment

The applicants will be assessed by an expert committee. The committee's mandate is to undertake an assessment of the applicants' qualifications based on the written material presented by the applicants, and the detailed description draw up for the position. A copy of the assessment report will be sent to all applicants. 

The applicants who are assessed as best qualified will be called to an interview. The interview should among other things, aim to clarify the applicant’s motivation and personal suitability for the position. A trial lecture may also be held.


General information

The appointment is made in accordance with State regulations and guidelines at UiT. At our website, you will find more information for applicants. 

The remuneration for Postdoctoral research fellow is in accordance with the State salary scale code 1352 with a gross annual salary ranging from NOK 650'-760' (in a 100% position). (In special cases, a higher salary may be considered.) A compulsory contribution of 2 % to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted. You will become a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund, which gives you many benefits in addition to a lifelong pension. Read more about your employee benefits at: spk.no.

The successful candidate must be willing to get involved in the ongoing development of their department and the university as a whole.

UiT wishes to promote gender equality. If two or more applicants are found to be equally qualified, the university will rank applicants from the underrepresented gender ahead of others.

According to the Norwegian Freedom and Information Act (Offentleglova) information about the applicant may be included in the public applicant list, also in cases where the applicant has requested non-disclosure. 


Om arbeidsgiveren:

UiT The Arctic University of Norway is a multi-campus research university and the northernmost university of the world. Our central location in the High North, our broad and diverse research and study portfolio, and our interdisciplinary qualities make us uniquely suited to meet the challenges of the future. At UiT you can explore global issues from a close-up perspective.

Credibility, academic freedom, closeness, creativity and commitment shall be hallmarks of the relationship between our employees, between our employees and our students and between UiT and our partners. 

The Faculty of Biosciences, Fisheries and Economics (BFE) consists of Department of Arctic and Marine Biology, Norwegian College of Fishery Science (NFH) and School of Business and Economics.The main task of BFE is to conduct teaching and research dissemination at a high national and international level within all relevant fields. Prioritized research areas are aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems, climate, life in the arctic, marine bioprospecting, fish health, seafood products, business and macroeconomics, resources and environment, markets and management of marine resources. The interdisciplinary profile of the faculty provides good opportunity to develop research projects involving several research groups at the faculty according to its strategy.
